segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: greatly disturbed that they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they seized them and put them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But many of those who had heard the word believed, and the number of the men came to about five thousand.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The next day their rulers, elders, and scribes gathered in Jerusalem,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: along with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and all who were of the high-priestly family,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they stood them in the middle and began to ask,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “By what power or by what name did you do this?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Rulers of the people and elders,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: if we are being examined today about a good deed done to a disabled man, by what means this man has been made well,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead—by him this man stands before you healthy.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: He is the stone scorned by you, the builders, which has become the cornerstone.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among people by which we must be saved.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John and grasped that they were unschooled and untrained men, they were amazed, and they recognized that they had been with Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And seeing the man who had been cured standing with them, they had nothing to say in reply.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they ordered them to go outside the council and conferred with one another,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What are we to do with these men? For that a remarkable sign has taken place through them is plain to all who live in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But so that it spreads no further among the people, let us threaten them, so that they no longer speak in this name to anyone at all.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they called them in and ordered them not to utter a word or teach at all in the name of Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Peter and John answered them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Whether it is right in God’s sight to listen to you rather than to God, you be the judges;

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: for we cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After threatening them further, they released them, finding no way to punish them because of the people, since all were glorifying God for what had happened;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for the man on whom this sign of healing had been performed was more than forty years old.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After their release they went to their own people and reported everything the chief priests and the elders had said to them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they heard it, they raised their voice together to God and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Master, you are the one who made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: who said by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of our father David, your servant: ‘Why did the Gentiles rage, and the peoples plot empty things?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Messiah.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For truly in this city they gathered together against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed—both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel—

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: to do whatever your hand and your plan had decided beforehand should happen.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant your slaves to speak your word with all boldness,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: while you stretch out your hand to heal, and signs and wonders take place through the name of your holy servant Jesus.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they had prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and went on speaking the word of God with boldness.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the community of those who had believed was one in heart and soul, and not one of them said that anything he possessed was his own, but they had everything in common.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With great power the apostles kept giving their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For there was no one in need among them, because all who owned land or houses would sell them and bring the proceeds of what was sold

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and lay them at the apostles’ feet, and it was distributed to each as anyone had need.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Joseph, whom the apostles called Barnabas—which translated means “son of encouragement”—a Levite, a Cypriot by birth,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: owned a field; he sold it, brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

notes.note: The Sadducees, the party of the priestly aristocracy, denied that the dead would be raised (Acts 23:8). The apostles were proclaiming that in the case of Jesus the resurrection had already happened, which challenged both the Sadducees’ teaching and their authority in the temple.

Annas had been deposed from the high priesthood by the Romans about fifteen years earlier; the officiating high priest at this time was his son-in-law Caiaphas. Luke gives Annas the title all the same (as in Luke 3:2), probably because he remained the head of the dominant high-priestly family. John and Alexander are otherwise unknown.

The Greek verb means both “heal” and “save,” and the same verb and its noun return in verse 12 as “saved” and “salvation.” Peter’s argument moves on that double sense: the name that restored this man’s body is the only one that rescues anyone. English needs two different words.

Peter alludes to Psalm 118:22, but the verb here is not the one the Greek Psalm uses for “rejected.” It means to treat as worthless or with contempt, and the translation keeps that sharper sense. Most versions use “rejected” to match the familiar wording of the Psalm.

The Greek is literally “head of the corner.” It may mean a foundation stone at the corner of a building or the capstone that completes it; scholars are divided. In either case it is the stone on which the structure depends.

The first word can mean “illiterate” but here more probably means that they lacked formal training in the Law such as the scribes had. The second describes a layperson or non-expert and carries no suggestion of stupidity. The council’s surprise is that men without credentials argue so boldly.

This is the adjective elsewhere rendered “righteous” or “just.” Here it stands in the impersonal expression “it is right,” for which English does not use “righteous,” so the traditional “right” is kept.

The word is not the usual one for “Lord” (which comes in verse 29) but the term for the master of a household or an absolute ruler. Most modern versions render it “Sovereign Lord” and the King James Version “Lord.” “Master” keeps it distinct and matches the believers’ description of themselves as his “slaves” in verse 29.

notes.phrase: by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of our father David, your servant
notes.note: The Greek of the earliest manuscripts is grammatically tangled at this point, and later manuscripts smooth it to “who by the mouth of your servant David said.” Many scholars suspect an early copying error. The translation gives the sense generally agreed on; the quotation is Psalm 2:1–2.

One Greek word means both “nations” and “Gentiles” (the non-Jewish peoples). English versions of the Psalm usually have “nations,” but “Gentiles” is used here because verse 27 applies the same word to the Romans who joined in condemning Jesus.

The Greek word means “anointed one” and in the Psalm refers to the Lord’s anointed king; older versions have “his Christ” and several modern ones “his Anointed.” “Messiah” is used because the title is the point. Verse 27 picks the word up with the related verb in “whom you anointed.”

The word can mean either “child” or “servant.” The King James Version has “child” here, but the same word is used of David in verse 25, and most scholars see an echo of the “servant of the Lord” in Isaiah, so “servant” is used for both.

The word is the ordinary Greek term for a slave, someone owned by a master, and differs from the word translated “servant” in verses 25, 27 and 30. Most versions soften it to “servants.” In the Greek Old Testament it is also an honorable self-description for those wholly at God’s disposal.

The word may mean God’s favor resting on the believers, or the goodwill of the people of Jerusalem toward them, as in Acts 2:47. The following verse, which begins with “for” and describes their generosity, fits either reading.

The Greek noun covers encouragement, comfort and exhortation, so “son of consolation” and “son of exhortation” are also possible. “Son of” is a Semitic way of describing a person’s character. Which Aramaic or Hebrew words lie behind Luke’s explanation of the name is uncertain.
